description: Intent i002 (debugfs-write-memdup-sscanf, snapshot s01) complete with 4 findings. (1) HIGH: drivers/net/ethernet/brocade/bna/bnad_debugfs.c:314-319, bnad_debugfs_write_regrd (debugfs .write at :454, registered at :521) — kern_buf = memdup_user(buf, nbytes) allocates exactly nbytes with no NUL terminator, then rc = sscanf(kern_buf, "%x:%x", &addr, &len) scans past the allocation when the user write contains no NUL (e.g. 'echo -n 1:2', nbytes=3); byte-for-byte sibling of the seed bfa bug in the same Brocade driver family; len bound applies to register count, not termination. (2) HIGH: bnad_debugfs.c:374-379, bnad_debugfs_write_regwr — same memdup_user(buf, nbytes) + sscanf(kern_buf, "%x:%x", &addr, &val); parsed addr/val also drive writel() to device MMIO; reg-offset mask/check does not provide string termination. (3) HIGH: drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_debugfs.c:170-184, ice_debugfs_module_write (debugfs 'module' file) — after count<=8 check, cmd_buf = memdup_user(buf, count) with no +1 slot, then sscanf(cmd_buf, "%s", user_val); 'echo -n disabled' (8 bytes, no newline) forces sscanf to read the 9th byte past the kmalloc(8) object; three sibling handlers share the pattern (nr_messages :260-264 count<=4, enable :335-339 count<=2, log_size :431-435 count<=5, all reported as candidates). (4) MEDIUM: drivers/s390/cio/cio_inject.c:98-102, crw_inject_write (debugfs 'crw_inject', crw_fops :150) — vmemdup_user(buf, lbuf) (kvmalloc+copy_from_user of exactly lbuf, verified in mm/util.c:236) then sscanf(buffer, "%x %x %x %x %x %x %x", ...) over seven tokens; unterminated write forces OOB read; medium because the file is mode 0200 and gated by a root-writable debugfs enable node (same root trust posture as the seed). Negative evidence: rvu_dbg_qsize_write (rvu_debugfs.c:1002) uses memdup_user(buffer, count + 1) plus explicit cmd_buf[count]='\0' — safe; rtw88 debug.c:173-192 helper memsets, copies at most size-1, and writes tmp[tmp_len]='\0' before sscanf — safe; rtw89_hex2bin_user uses bounded hex2bin, not a string consumer — safe; qib flash_write is fixed-size binary; wfx hif/wlcore/wil6210/blkrx are binary consumers; wil6210 sscanf/kstrtol handlers use memdup_user_nul; regmap-debugfs kmalloc(count) sites are read-side output buffers, not usercopy input. Bounded limitations: only the debugfs write branch was audited (sysfs/proc/ioctl covered by i003-i005); the 206-site memdup_user sweep flagged string consumers per enclosing function but simple_write_to_buffer fixed-array debugfs handlers (ath10k/ath11k/ixgbe/hisilicon/xgbe/habanalabs/mtk_vcodec/adf_heartbeat/powernv-eeh/moxtet/turris-mox/i915) were enumerated, not individually audited; kmalloc(count)+copy_from_user sweep was only partially triaged (nvram.c:241, es2.c:1123, i2c-dev.c:145 unread); wfx_send_pds consumption (wfx/debug.c:216) and rtw89 sscanf write helpers (lines 149/226/272/326/1004/1115) remain unresolved; evidence is static only (no build/KASAN reproducer). Final artifact with literal verified quotes: agent-state/findings/i002.json.
